en.title: Man who killed 13 in Fort Hood mass shooting to be executed by Army firing squad
en.summary: The Pentagon's defense secretary recommended and President Trump approved the execution of a man convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood.

stories.title: Ex-Army major who killed 13 at Fort Hood set to be executed by firing squad

en.title: Ex-Army major who killed 13 at Fort Hood set to be executed by firing squad
en.summary: A former Army major convicted of a Fort Hood mass shooting will be executed by military firing squad, the first such execution by the U.S. military since World War II.

en.summary: The Supreme Court heard arguments in a case where Boulder, Colorado seeks to hold energy companies responsible for climate change damages, with the justices considering whether to allow the lawsuit to proceed.

stories.title: Inside the cases the Supreme Court will take up this term

en.summary: The Supreme Court began its new term and will address cases involving voting rights, gun control, and whether federal law prevents states from holding oil companies liable in climate disputes.

en.title: Facing Backlash, Trump Says His Super PAC Will Pay for Taxpayer-Funded Ads

en.summary: The Singapore dollar remained stable against the U.S. dollar in Asian trading. The currency's movement will continue to depend on U.S. dollar performance and Treasury yield developments.

stories.title: Opposing Forces Keep Oil Prices in Narrow Range

en.title: Opposing Forces Keep Oil Prices in Narrow Range
en.summary: Oil prices are trading in a narrow band as improving Middle Eastern crude supply conflicts with ongoing U.S.-Iran tensions. These opposing factors prevent significant price movement.

en.title: Oil Is Flowing From Hormuz Again—Just Not the Kind the World Needs Most
en.summary: Global markets face elevated fuel prices due to damaged refineries and tight diesel supplies despite renewed oil flows from the Hormuz region. Diesel shortages are driving the scramble for fuel worldwide.
